name: Richard S. Fuld Jr.

summary.text: Richard S. Fuld Jr. was chairman and chief executive of Lehman Brothers Holdings when it filed for bankruptcy in September 2008. The court-appointed bankruptcy examiner, Anton Valukas, reported in March 2010 that 'colorable claims' existed against Fuld and three former chief financial officers over the non-disclosure of the firm's 'Repo 105' transactions, which temporarily removed tens of billions of dollars from Lehman's balance sheet at quarter-ends. Fuld told Congress in April 2010 that he had no recollection of Repo 105 documents. He and other former Lehman officers settled a shareholder class action in 2011 for $90 million, paid from insurance.

facts.claim: The Lehman bankruptcy examiner's March 2010 report found that colorable claims of breach of fiduciary duty existed against Richard Fuld and former chief financial officers Chris O'Meara, Erin Callan and Ian Lowitt, and a colorable claim of professional malpractice against auditor Ernst & Young, in connection with the Repo 105 transactions.
facts.quote: colorable claims of breach of fiduciary duty exist against Richard Fuld, Chris O'Meara, Erin Callan, and Ian Lowitt, and a colorable claim of professional malpractice exists against Ernst & Young

facts.claim: The examiner concluded that Lehman's business decisions were largely within the business judgment rule, but that the decision not to disclose their effects gave rise to colorable claims against the senior officers who oversaw and certified the financial statements.
facts.quote: decision not to disclose the effects of these judgments does give rise to colorable claims against the senior officers who oversaw and certified misleading financial statements

sources.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs
sources.title: Testimony of Anton R. Valukas, Examiner, Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc.

facts.claim: According to the examiner, Repo 105 transactions were booked as sales rather than financings and removed about $39 billion from Lehman's balance sheet at the end of the fourth quarter of 2007, $49 billion in the first quarter of 2008 and $50 billion in the second quarter of 2008.
facts.quote: "shed" about $39 billion from its balance sheet at the end of the fourth quarter of 2007, $49 billion in the first quarter of 2008 and $50 billion in the second quarter

sources.title: Report details how Lehman hid its woes

facts.claim: The examiner's report described Fuld as denying knowledge of the Repo 105 transactions while recalling that he issued directives to reduce the firm's debt levels.
facts.quote: Fuld is described in the examiner's report as denying having knowledge of the Repo 105 transactions, though he recalled issuing several directives to reduce the firm's debt levels.

sources.title: Report details how Lehman hid its woes

facts.claim: At an April 2010 House hearing, Fuld said he had 'absolutely no recollection whatsoever' of documents relating to Repo 105; his lawyer said Fuld did not structure or negotiate the transactions and was not aware of their accounting treatment. SEC Chairman Mary Schapiro said the agency was examining the truthfulness of Lehman's disclosures.
facts.quote: Fuld said he had "absolutely no recollection whatsoever" of any documents related to the so-called Repo 105 accounting maneuver.

facts.claim: In 2011 former Lehman officers including Fuld reached a $90 million settlement, funded by directors-and-officers insurance, of a shareholder class action begun in June 2008; underwriters later settled the same litigation for $417 million and Ernst & Young for $99 million.
facts.quote: Lehman's former officers, including ex-Chief Executive Richard Fuld, settled for $90m

openQuestions: Site claim that Fuld 'demanded aggressive quarterly leverage reductions': partly supported; the examiner's report records Fuld recalling directives to reduce debt levels, while he denied knowledge of Repo 105 itself.
Site claim that senior management received large stock awards and bonuses while reporting misleading leverage: not tested here; no source on compensation was found.
Site claim that E&Y paid $10 million to the New York Attorney General: not tested; only the $99 million investor settlement was found.
Whether the SEC ever formally closed its Repo 105 inquiry without charging Fuld could not be confirmed from a primary source.
The examiner's full report text was not retrieved; the findings above rest on his Senate testimony and contemporaneous coverage.
